root.label: Margaret Hamilton joins MIT Apollo software project

events.label: Margaret Hamilton joins MIT Apollo software project

slots.name: application date
slots.sentence: She began working at MIT soon afterwards, and in 1965 applied to join a lab at the university that was seeking people to develop software to "send a man to the moon."

slots.name: NASA contracts
slots.sentence: The lab had won a contract from NASA to build the onboard flight software for the Apollo program.

slots.name: first programmer
slots.sentence: Hamilton was hired as the first programmer for the project, MIT said, adding that she was also the project's first female programmer.

slots.name: team lead promotion
slots.sentence: She initially worked on the first software for the uncrewed Apollo missions, before being promoted to lead the team developing on-board flight software for the crewed missions.

slots.name: software staff count
slots.sentence: "By 1968, she was assistant director in charge of (Apollo's) Command and Service Module team, and more than 400 people were working on Apollo's software," MIT said.

slots.name: published papers
slots.sentence: Hamilton published more than 130 papers and went on to start her own software companies Higher Order Software and Hamilton Technologies.

slots.name: move to Boston
slots.sentence: Hamilton studied mathematics before moving to Boston, Massachusetts, in 1959.
